# LIMES

<!-- Generated by tools/generate_runtime_docs.py; regenerate after changing the contract. -->

**An evidence-backed world model for German and European policy research.**

LIMES connects official registries, agency dispatches, curated reporting and coded
event observations in a shared, queryable model of entities, relationships and
change. It brings AI-assisted extraction,
ontology-driven knowledge representation and visual investigation into one
research platform, turning fragmented public information into a connected view
that analysts can explore and inspect.

Follow a relationship across sources, place it in its geographic context and
trace how it changes over time. A PySide6 desktop workspace brings network,
geographic and temporal views together, while natural-language questions open a
path into the graph through validated, read-only queries.

## From public information to connected intelligence

- **Build a shared model.** Registry records and source-attributed news claims feed an
  ontology-driven Neo4j knowledge graph. Entity resolution links records across
  sources so research can follow relationships beyond individual documents.
- **Investigate in context.** Explore connections through the desktop's network,
  map and timeline views. Use natural language, a visual query builder or Cypher
  to approach the same graph from different research questions.
- **Follow developments across sources.** Investigate proposals, announcements,
  denials, agreements and later official confirmation. Attribution, modality,
  event lifecycle and temporal precision remain visible beside the evidence.
- **Understand what changed, and when.** Bitemporal assertions distinguish when a
  claim was valid from when it was recorded. Conflicting claims are preserved,
  keeping disagreement and evolving knowledge available for analysis.
- **Keep the evidence within reach.** Provenance connects claims to their
  immutable dispatch versions, text spans or coded export rows. Corrections and
  syndication retain their lineage; copied reports do not become independent
  corroboration. A content-addressed archive remains the system of record.
  Hop-level coverage and diagnosis accompany empty results, helping researchers
  assess where evidence may be missing.
- **Operate through a consistent interface.** Authenticated HTTP connects the
  desktop and remote CLI to queries and durable operator jobs, from ingestion
  and backfill to physical backup.

A typical investigation moves from a question to a set of connected entities,
then through their relationships, locations and history to the underlying
sources. The result is a world model whose evidence and gaps remain visible
throughout the research process.

LIMES is a personal research artifact. Source coverage is uneven and extracted
claims can be wrong; inspect provenance and hop-level coverage when interpreting
results. Public-person data has no automatic retention policy.

The design, specifications and [two delivery sequences](docs/ROADMAP.md) describe
one integrated product. Read this page as the complete product overview; consult
the [documentation map](docs/INDEX.md), backend/desktop package registers and
[verification status](docs/TESTING_PHASE.md) for implementation and acceptance
status. Those records distinguish current artifacts, evidence gaps and open repairs.

## Architecture and runtime

| Runtime fact | Current contract |
|---|---|
| Shipped services | api, neo4j, worker |
| API publication | `127.0.0.1:8000:8000` |
| Database publication | None |
| API authentication | Bearer token |
| Desktop credentials | Session memory only |
| Spending enforcement | None |
| Service user | `7474:7474` |
| Operations authentication | Separate operator bearer token |
| Host Docker socket | Absent |
| Backup control | Private authenticated HTTP |
| Deployment | Recorded immutable image IDs |

The [core design](docs/LIMES_Design_Document_v2.0.0.md) and
[technical specification](docs/LIMES_Technical_Specification_v2.1.0.md) define the
system, including integrated agency/news intelligence.
[Desktop architecture](docs/LIMES_Desktop_Client_Architecture_v1.0.0.md) defines
its API consumer. Shared adapters, archive, extraction, entity/event
resolution and ontology validation feed one Neo4j graph with native vectors.
The worker owns processing; the desktop owns visual investigation through the API.
[Runtime architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [operations](docs/OPERATIONS.md) and
[verification](docs/TESTING_PHASE.md) document the current executable contract.

Stack administration and ordinary use are separate. Administrators build/start
containers; consumers need only an API credential and HTTP client. Operators use a
separate credential to submit durable jobs through HTTP, including backup. No
service is root, holds a Docker socket, or invokes Docker. Named volumes hold all
mutable service data; host configuration stays owned by its operator and read-only
in containers. The retired Dash service is absent.

## Getting started

Initialize with `python3 tools/init_config.py` (requires the host `acl` utility).
Set the OpenRouter key privately in `config/secrets.env`. For a disposable local
stack, run `docker compose --env-file config/settings.env --env-file
config/secrets.env -f docker-compose.yml up -d --build`. For a release, use
`python3 tools/deploy.py` from a clean committed checkout; see OPERATIONS.

### Desktop access

Launch the desktop with `venv/bin/limes-desktop` after installing the workspace
dependencies shown under Verification below.

Desktop: use `http://127.0.0.1:8000` locally, HTTPS remotely, or a loopback SSH
forward (`ssh -N -L 8000:127.0.0.1:8000 account@server`). The SSH account needs no
Docker membership. Profiles never store credentials. Use the operator credential
for desktop backup; a consumer token cannot submit operational jobs.

### Remote operations

```bash
# On the client; supply the operator token in the environment, never an argument.
export LIMES_REMOTE_URL=https://your-api.example
venv/bin/limes remote run ingest --source gleif
venv/bin/limes remote run backfill --source gdelt --days 30
venv/bin/limes remote run backup
venv/bin/limes remote status JOB_UUID --wait
```

## Model selection and usage accounting

There is no cost governor or budget envelope. Calls record model, purpose, tokens
and cost. Real ingestion, backfill and model measurement are operator actions;
tests mock all paid transports. Provisional selection validates catalogue IDs and
pins the date; measured selection scores all four roles and publishes a complete
report and pins only after successful scoring. Worker pins live in the named
models volume, separate from host secrets; the API refreshes atomic pins before
its next NL query without an administrator restart.

## Verification

Use affected tests and shared invariant checks during development, one full
pre-merge candidate run, and lightweight checks for documentation, per AGENTS.md.
The commands below are the full verification inventory.

```bash
UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=venv uv sync --frozen --all-packages
venv/bin/ruff check src tests desktop/src desktop/tests
venv/bin/mypy
venv/bin/python tools/check_docs.py docs/
venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit -q
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen venv/bin/python -m pytest desktop/tests/unit desktop/tests/contract -q
venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/integration -q
venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/acceptance -q
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen venv/bin/python -m pytest desktop/tests/integration -q
```

Graph tests own disposable databases and clean them up. Acceptance runs separately
because of its nested plugin. GitHub Actions runs these suites and retains JUnit
results. Read AGENTS.md, the documentation index, both package registers, the newest five
DECISIONS entries, and OPEN_ISSUES.md on
re-entry. Never treat cached remote refs as a live Git baseline.
